title: Make LocalFlatHead optimizer-visible and checkpoint-stable
decision: Yes, with a documented capacity limit: the flat action head is now genuinely trainable, serializable, and reproducible under a dynamic action vocabulary via an explicit materialize()/checkpoint contract, but it remains an O(distinct semantic actions) table with no unseen-action generalization.
hypothesis: Registered parameter containers plus explicit pre-optimizer materialization yield nonzero gradients, optimizer updates, and exact checkpoint round trips without changing fixture scores.
implementation_summary: LocalFlatHead.action_embeddings is now an nn.ParameterDict (was a plain Python dict invisible to model.parameters()/named_parameters()).

canonical_action_key(action) derives a semantic key independent of opaque reference ids (dsl.operators.legal_set reserved 'OPERATOR <op> <slot>=<kind>:<request_id>:<opaque_id>' serialization collapses to '<slot>=<kind>') and independent of candidate order/list position; plain (non-operator) action identities pass through unchanged, preserving every existing fixture harness's behavior.

LocalFlatHead.materialize(action_views) pre-registers one parameter per canonical key, deduplicating, and must run before optimizer construction. After materialize(), an unseen canonical key either raises (unseen_action_policy='error', default) or routes to a dedicated '__unk__' parameter (unseen_action_policy='unk') -- it never silently lazily allocates a parameter the optimizer cannot see.
Before materialize() (fixture/wiring mode), unseen actions still lazily allocate exactly as before DSH3-21, so zero-step fixture numeric behavior is unchanged.

checkpoint_state()/load_checkpoint_state() add an explicit CHECKPOINT_FORMAT_VERSION and fail closed (raise ValueError/RuntimeError) on format_version mismatch, action-registry mismatch (vocabulary must match exactly before loading), or tensor shape mismatch (torch's own strict=True state_dict load).
score() rejects (ValueError) legal_actions whose canonical keys collide within one call, instead of silently scoring one of the duplicates.

notes: oracle pass recovered every correct action

candidate_reference_permutation.note: Verified in tests/test_models/test_local_action_head.py::test_local_flat_head_candidate_order_permutation_stable (score depends on action identity, not its position in legal_actions) and test_canonical_action_key_drops_opaque_reference_ids / test_local_flat_head_opaque_id_only_change_shares_one_parameter (opaque reference-id permutation collapses to one parameter).

stop_rule_applied: The flat head inherently requires an unbounded per-action parameter table (no compositional structure over action identity). Per the issue's stop rule, it is kept and documented as a non-generalizing diagnostic/baseline head -- capacity is O(distinct semantic actions) -- rather than forcing a fake generalization claim. Heads with bounded capacity over an unbounded vocabulary already exist in this module (TernaryDigitHead, TernaryECOCHead, GrammarFactorizedHead).
non_goals: No unseen-action generalization claim for LocalFlatHead.
Opaque reference ids are never used as vocabulary/scoring authority; canonical_action_key strips them by construction.
No legal-membership changes: decode() still only ever returns an action_identity present in the supplied legal_actions (or None).

tests.also_run: tests/test_harnesses/quantization/test_sensitivity.py, tests/test_harnesses/quantization/test_calibration.py, tests/test_harnesses/experiments/test_cap3_03_ternary_falsification.py, tests/test_harnesses/experiments/test_cap2_04_state_ablation.py (all downstream LocalFlatHead consumers) -- 47 passed after updating test_sensitivity.py's test_baseline_parameters_restored_after_profiling to warm the head's action embeddings before snapshotting baseline parameters, since those embeddings are now real named_parameters() entries instead of being invisible outside a plain dict

version_stamp_bump.reason: src/slm_training/models/local_action_head.py is a watched path for this component; the ParameterDict/materialize/checkpoint change is not behavior-neutral (it changes named_parameters() membership and adds fail-closed checkpoint validation), so this is a real bump, not a no-bump note.

honest_caveats: This is a CPU fixture/unit-test verification, not a production TwoTowerModel training integration or ship-gate run; no checkpoint bucket sync or MODEL_CARD update applies (no checkpoint was created/promoted).

canonical_action_key only strips the opaque request_id/opaque_id pair from the reserved operator serialization format; it does not resolve a reference's semantic_fingerprint from a live ReferenceTableV1 (out of scope for this head -- it has no access to one). Two structurally different references of the same kind in the same slot still collapse onto one parameter; this is a precision limit, not full compositional action identity.
GlobalMaskedHead, TernaryDigitHead, TernaryECOCHead, and GrammarFactorizedHead were not touched; this issue is scoped to LocalFlatHead only.

notes: oracle pass recovered every correct action
